title: Preserving Digital History: How to Close the Web's 'Memory Hole'

reader_summary.headline: Hi, welcome to the A16Z podcast, I'm Zorn.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, welcome to the A16Z podcast, I'm Zorn. Conventional wisdom has it that most everything important is accessible online, and that it will exist forever. But in fact, more than 98% of the information on the web is lost within 20 years, and huge gaps exist in our cultural history.

key_points.text: This includes published works like news reports, books, music, and video.

key_points.text: A16Z investment partner Alex Pruden and I interviewed Brewster Kale and Sam Williams, who are using different approaches to attack this problem.

thesis: The podcast argues that over 98% of web information is lost within 20 years, creating a 'memory hole' that erases crucial cultural history and enables political erasure of the past. It posits that preserving digital history is essential for maintaining accountability, preventing the rewriting of history, and ensuring societies have reliable context to function amidst fake news and government manipulation.
